For each task type, a model from each provider. If you have subscriptions, use them first; when one runs out of quota, move to the next column. Speed picks the fastest setting that meets the goal; Cost the cheapest.

OMP discoveries and fixes

OMP has its own tools to read, search and edit files. They are faster and use less context than the shell. Many models, especially the Anthropic ones, do not use them, even when the prompt tells them to. It seems that habits from model training work against the harness the model runs in. The visible cost: OMP rejects an edit on lines that the model read through the shell.

The block that stops shell reads, the Bash Interceptor, is off by default in OMP, so every OMP user can have this problem.

What we changed

ChangeWhy
Bash Interceptor on for all modelsShell reads and searches are blocked with a message that names the right tool.
Six tool rules merged into the Tool Policy of all three system promptsModels now get the rules that were missing.
Subagent LSP on; Encourage Edits offEncourage Edits has no effect with our SYSTEM.md.
Per-model guidance and short coordinator checks on in intelligent-auto-agentsTwo lines that only repeated the system prompt are off. Each check asks the coordinator for one small action: from the report, or one cheap command.
Live settings saved into the tracked profileThe profile now matches what runs.

Known limits

  1. The block does not cover shell commands run inside the eval tool.
  2. Subagent LSP and the review notes are on but not measured.

Key takeaways

Results are a guide, not a benchmark: 12 real tasks (4 per type) plus small tasks, all run in our own harness and repositories.

  1. Claude Sonnet 5.5 high beats Claude Opus 5.5 low: grade 4.67 against 4.58, with both passing 33 of 33.
  2. More effort helps Anthropic models most: from lowest to highest effort the grade rises for Sonnet 5.5 (4.17 to 4.67) and Claude Haiku 5.5 (4.00 to 4.94), and only a little for GPT-6.1 Sol (Sol 6.1) (4.25 to 4.33) and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (DS V4.1 Flash) (4.62 to 4.67).
  3. Use Haiku 5.5 at high effort or above for graded work: at high it grades 4.44 on feature work and 4.75 on moderate tasks and passes every check; at low and medium it misses the goal on both.
  1. Use Sol 6.1, not GPT-6.2 Sol (Sol 6.2): at low effort both grade 4.25, but Sol 6.2 passes fewer checks (30 vs 33 of 33) and is slower (148 s vs 127 s).
  2. GPT-6 Luna (Luna 6) against GPT-5.6 Luna (Luna 5.6) is mixed: Luna 6 grades higher at extra high (4.00 vs 3.00) and lower at max (3.92 vs 4.12), and is slower (546 s vs 381 s at extra high).
  3. Luna 6 at low and medium effort is not fit for coding: it grades 2.00 and 1.92. In the latest round Luna 6 passed only 81% to 82% of tasks.
  4. GPT-6.2 Astra (Astra 6.2) low passed 33 of 33 but is one of the slowest settings, at 21 tokens a second.
  5. GPT-6.1 Terra (Terra 6.1) medium is fine for coding: its feature-work grade is 4.06, it passed all 19 feature-work checks, and 11 of 12 in the latest round. On one task it repeatedly left a percentage unrounded (worst task 2.0), so review its output formatting.
  1. Effort changes Haiku 5.5 and Luna 6 much more than Sonnet 5.5. From low to extra high, Haiku 5.5 grades 4.00 to 4.94 and takes 97 s to 274 s per task. From low to max, Luna 6 passes 48% to 79% of checks and takes 106 s to 709 s. Sonnet 5.5 from low to high: 4.17 to 4.67, 41 s to 68 s.
  2. Haiku 5.5 at extra high is strong and cheap for coding: grade 4.94, 43 of 44 checks passed, $3.15 for 12 tasks against $3.98 for Sonnet 5.5 high. Its runs are long: 274 s per task against 68 s.
  3. Luna 5.6 and Luna 6 also change a lot with effort, but even at their best they trail Haiku 5.5 at extra high (grades 4.12 and 4.00 against 4.94). Do not run them below extra high.
  1. Use DS V4.1 Flash at low effort, not high: on feature work low grades 4.60 against 4.20, passes 40 of 40 checks against 38, and takes 6:00 per pass against 9:38.
  2. Tencent Hy4 Flash (HY4 Flash) at high effort meets the goal on all three task types. At low effort it misses it on feature work.
  3. Use Grok 4.6, not 4.7: quality is about equal (tools test pass 98% against 98%–100%), but 4.6 needs fewer round trips (12.8 against 16.8 at low, 15.1 against 22.4 at high) and is faster (67 s against 94 s at low, 151 s against 340 s at high); for feature work use 4.6 at high effort.
  1. Raising the tool-output limit lowered round trips per run for every model tested, by 3% to 36%. If a tool or extension shortens tool output (for example Pare, RTK and similar), aggressive truncation can make some models take many more round trips, especially HY4 Flash (44 against 28 per run at high) and GLM 5.3 Flash (32 against 21 at low).
  2. Some bugs are found by GPT models and not by Anthropic models, so review with more than one model family. On one task, a wrong-branch fix, Astra 6.2 low, Sol 6.1 medium, Terra 6.1 medium and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash low fixed it 3 of 3 times; Opus 5.5 medium and Sonnet 5.5 medium 0 of 3; Opus 5.5 low and Sonnet 5.5 high 1 of 3. This is one task only.
  3. Tell Terra 6.1 “You may not delegate.” in the brief. Without it, it hands small tasks to helper agents and waits. In our runs, 0 of 140 runs delegate with it.
  4. A line asking DS V4.1 Flash to send independent reads together in one reply helped: round trips 30.5 to 26.7; time 232 to 185 s; pass 100% to 98%.
